text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on prod after yesterday's batching heuristic change. Latency P95 for long-context (seq ~1536) jumps ~2.5x. Traces attached (nsys).

kevin: Which part regressed? matmul kernels or more memory thrash?

maria: Matmul. nsys timeline shows cublasLt matmul falling back to a different algo that needs a big workspace. Before patch it used algo ID 42 (no extra ws). After patch most requests pick algo 7 which requests ~200MB workspace and triggers workspace allocation stalls.

perf-bot: nsys summary (extracted):
```
Kernel Type         Calls   Total Time(ms)   Avg(ms)   Max(ms)
cublasLtMatmul       312    12560.4           40.2      123.1
sgemm                124    148.1             1.19      3.2
memcpy_htod           89    102.4             1.15      4.6
```

maria: The timeline snippet shows repeated workspace reallocs (cudaMalloc/cudaFree) interleaved with matmul calls — looks like our batching heuristic created larger per-batch shapes (N increased) making matmul choose a workspace-heavy algo.

alex: Repro steps?

maria: Quick repro: run the perf harness with the new batching heuristic enabled and a synthetic workload: `REDWOOD_FEATURE_BATCH_HEURISTIC=v2 ./bin/perf_harness --profile nsys --seq 1536 --batch 4 --model gpt-j-slim`

kevin: I can repro locally. If I force cublasLt workspace limit lower (`CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_LIMIT_BYTES=67108864`) it falls back to the cheaper algo and latency returns to baseline. So it's definitely an algo selection + workspace sizing problem.

dina: Is KV cache behavior involved? Did the change cause more fused requests so KV cache entries grew and increased effective matmul dims?

maria: Yes — heuristic started grouping requests by remaining tokens left to generate (to improve throughput), which increases aggregated seq length in many batches when KV cache hits are high. That bumps the matmul shapes from (B*H, S, D) proportional dims and causes different algorithm picks.

tom: Could also be cuBLASLt deterministic probe path timing out and choosing a safe algo when workspace probe fails under contention. Any probe logs?

perf-bot: From the probe traces: `cublasLtMatmul` probe returned status CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED twice for algo 42 under high concurrency, then selected algo 7. Probe timeouts line up with times we saw malloc/free spikes.

alex: Two immediate mitigations: 1) cap the batching heuristic so aggregated seq*N doesn't exceed X, 2) set an algorithm preference list forcing algo 42 for these shapes. But forcing can be brittle across GPU types.

kevin: Agreed. Another approach: preallocate a small slab pool for matmul workspace to avoid cudaMalloc churn — reduces probe-induced stalls. Slab pool size ~256MB per stream reduced the malloc/free overhead in my local run.

maria: Notes from nsys perfetto view: heatmap shows matmul kernels at 60–80% occupancy but stalls at `cudaMalloc` markers. Perf regressions align with workspace allocation latency spikes. Link to perfetto trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace#fake-link-184500 (internal)

dina: Do we need to revert the heuristic immediately? What's impact on overall throughput?

maria: Throughput improved for short seq (<512) but regressed for long seq workloads. Customer impact: 2 customers reported higher tail latencies for long-context chat sessions. We should rollback the heuristic rollout to canary while we fix.

kevin: I'll open a small PR to add a safety cap to the grouping and disable for sequences >1024. Also adding `--ws-slab` flag to perf harness and a configuration knob `matmul.workspace_slab_size`.

maria: Also let's add a runtime guard that prefers the non-workspace algorithm for (seq>=1024, batch<=8) shapes, and log when falling back to algo with large workspace so we can alert.

tom: I'll prototype the slab allocator in the runtime. Plan: pre-reserve per-device slab, suballocate for matmul workspaces, and only fallback to cudaMalloc if slab exhausted. Should cut allocation latency and improve probe reliability.

dina: Can we add an integration test that runs a stress scenario (mixed seq distribution) and asserts P95 < X? Put this in CI perf stage.

maria: Yes, add perf regression check, and include a short nsys timeline upload artifact. For now, rolling back the heuristic rollout and deploying kevin's cap patch is the action.

kevin: I'll queue the rollback + cap patch. Leaving TODOs in the PR: (1) metric on `algo_workshop_fallbacks`, (2) slab allocator prototype, (3) runtime probing timeouts logging.

maria: Thanks all — will file a customer-facing incident note and ping support.

perf-bot: Action items created: INF-3421 (rollback heuristic canary), INF-3422 (slab allocator prototyping), INF-3423 (probe/logging). :white_check_mark:

kevin: Follow-up: I've attached a small nsys capture snippet (gzipped) to the ticket with labeled kernel timestamps.

alex: Great. Once slab allocator landed we should re-run the matmul algo sweep with the probe disabled to produce a preferred algorithm map per shape/gpu.

maria: Agreed — we'll also update Optimize to suggest different batch configurations to avoid workspace-heavy algos for long-context use cases.

kevin: FYI: CUDA/CuBLAS driver versions matter — I saw different default picks on 12.2 vs 12.3. Include that in testing matrix.

maria: Done. Closing thread for now, follow-ups in the INF tickets.
